tweets.text:
A year ago we launched Opus 4.5, the first model to write 100% of my code.

Shipping PRs hasn’t caught up, so today we’re launching Claude Ship in beta for Team and Enterprise. I use it all day every day and can’t imagine shipping without it. https://t.co/IfK0Oua6rZ

It multiplies my velocity. I don’t need to wait around for code review or babysit PRs, and the results are better.
Code Review looks for bugs, PR Steward works on fixes and failing checks, and Claude Approvals approves what your team’s policy allows (the last two are in beta).

Anyone can use /ship. If you’re on a Team or Enterprise plan, your admin can turn on Claude Ship per GitHub repo. I’d start with one repo and run Approvals in observe mode until you trust it.

https://t.co/p0T6zDSIwM

Part of the disconnect is that the name “data” massively undersells what it truly represents in model development.

People who are not close to model development think of data as this  inert commodity you buy and shovel into a model, like coal.

In reality great data encodes incredibly high value knowledge, taste and expertise, often articulated and structured in ways that did not exist previously. 

This makes it one of THE fundamental building blocks for creating increasingly capable intelligence across domains. 

Data will continue to be incredibly central to the intelligence industry .

Great meeting with VP @JDVance on Friday to discuss American AI leadership, cybersecurity, and modernizing our nation’s software infrastructure.

We also discussed an issue close to my heart: American leadership in open-weight AI.

tweets.summary_en: The U.S. could lead in frontier AI and still lose influence over the global AI ecosystem if it falls behind in open-weight models. Allies seeking control over their own AI infrastructure are increasingly turning to Chinese models, while U.S. startups need a competitive domestic ecosystem.

tweets.text: The man is severely underpaid. https://t.co/tPp4K55neH

New research from Replit on scaling laws for agent swarms. 

We show that scaling the number of agents can yield dramatic performance gains, but unlike traditional scaling laws, more compute doesn't necessarily translate into better results, and how agents organize themselves matters.

- Given a fixed two-hour window, Opus 5.5 went from a 3.7x speedup on NumPy with one agent to 18.9x with 32 agents.

- GPT-6.2 Astra was the strongest solo agent but exhibited negative scaling beyond 8 agents.

- Models spontaneously developed different organizational structures. Decentralized swarms scaled better than those that relied on centralized coordination.

- The parallelizability of the problem was a strong predictor of swarm performance.

- Interestingly, individual model intelligence is a poor predictor of collective intelligence.

We’re also open-sourcing Optimization-Bench to advance research into this new dimension of inference-time scaling.

https://t.co/RXBU7aM5FE
tweets.summary_en: Replit found that adding agents can dramatically speed up tasks that split into parallel work, especially when agents coordinate independently. The strongest solo model got worse beyond eight agents, showing that solo performance is a poor predictor of how a swarm will scale.

tweets.text: 2026 is just waking up each day to the magnitude of news that could only have happened once per decade before 2026.

This is a pretty key insight. Services businesses are always held back by their ability to deliver outcomes to customers. 

That scaling essentially only could come from headcount, and no matter how much demand you saw, there was always a finite amount of talent you could get for the problem you were going after. Not to mention, the customer generally always wants the work done faster, at a lower price, or at a higher quality.

Agents entirely change the calculus here, because now we can scale output in a way that’s decoupled from the among of time that goes in. A single engineer can have the output of dozens of engineers before. A single designer can probably build out your entire design system and brand. And so on.

Well why isn’t this just all agents then? Because the key is to still have experts on the front end that actually can ensure the right outcomes are delivered from agents.

It’s likely that we’re going to see this in a wide variety of categories. You’ll see this in cyber security, advertising and marketing, legal, accounting, IT transformation, and a number of other historically people-only services industries.

It’s a great time if you’re starting one of these businesses, or if you have the capability to transform an existing one.
tweets.summary_en: AI agents could let service businesses increase output without adding headcount at the same rate. Human experts still need to guide the work and verify that it delivers what customers need.

builders.summary_en: Jokes that LinkedIn will catch up to Jensen Huang's return a week late
builders.summary_zh: 调侃 LinkedIn 会晚一周为黄仁勋回归沸腾

keywords.definition_zh: 指因兴奋或震惊而反应特别强烈。
keywords.example_zh: 作者调侃 LinkedIn 上的人会为 Jensen 回归的消息沸腾，只不过要到下周才听到。

tweets.text: People on LinkedIn are going to go WILD when they hear about Jensen returning, next week
BREAKING: AI JESUS IS RISEN

builders.name: Zara Zhang
builders.headline_zh: 每天发帖也能保护隐私，只分享愿意公开的内容
builders.headline_en: You can post daily and still keep your life private

points.zh: 几乎每天发帖，也只公开生活和想法中约 1% 的内容。选题标准是自己愿意公开，同时别人也有兴趣。
points.en: She posts almost daily and estimates that she shares less than 1% of her life and thoughts. She picks material that others may find interesting and that she is comfortable making public.

builders.summary_en: You can post daily and still keep your life private
builders.summary_zh: 每天发帖也能保护隐私，只分享愿意公开的内容

slang.definition_en: Generic or low-quality content churned out by AI.
slang.definition_zh: AI 批量生成的粗糙、同质化内容。

keywords.definition_zh: 比喻一个人的生活或想法完全摊开，别人很容易看透。
keywords.example_zh: 作者说，有人以为每天在社交媒体发帖就得把整个生活摊开，她自己只分享愿意公开的一小部分。

keywords.definition_zh: 比喻从整体中分出来的极小一部分。
keywords.example_zh: 作者用它来形容自己公开的生活和想法，估计连百分之一都不到。

keywords.definition_zh: 是对粗糙、套路化的 AI 生成内容的贬称。
keywords.example_zh: 作者在另一条推文里分享了如何避免 AI 生成的设计显得粗糙或千篇一律，读者无需有设计师背景。

tweets.text:
You can post on social media every day and still be a very private person; the two are not contradictory 

Many people have the misconception that sharing your thoughts online means turning your whole life into an open book for others to see. This can’t be further from the truth

I post almost every day but I only share a tiny sliver of my life & thoughts, probably less than 1%. I only share what I’m comfortable with sharing

The key is to find out which 1% is at the intersection of “interesting to others” and “comfortable for you”
tweets.summary_en: Posting daily can coexist with privacy. Share the small slice of your life or thinking that others will find interesting and that you feel comfortable making public.

tweets.text: How to prevent AI slop in design (without being a designer): https://t.co/xKfBQTQXns https://t.co/49RO5JiyR1

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.headline_zh: 调侃2027年的工作都围着 AI 智能体转
builders.headline_en: Jokes that every 2027 job will revolve around AI agent swarms

points.zh: 给 2027 年的岗位改名开玩笑，让创始人统领 AI 智能体群，产品经理指挥它们，设计师给它们编排动作。
points.en: He imagines tongue-in-cheek 2027 job titles in which founders command AI agent swarms, product managers steer them, and designers choreograph them.

builders.summary_en: Jokes that every 2027 job will revolve around AI agent swarms
builders.summary_zh: 调侃2027年的工作都围着 AI 智能体转

slang.definition_en: A group of AI agents coordinating work.
slang.definition_zh: 一起分工协作的 AI 智能体群。

slang.definition_en: An engineer who works closely with customers to implement and adapt a product.
slang.definition_zh: 深入客户现场，负责产品部署和适配的工程师。

keywords.definition_zh: 是对负责调度和管住一群智能体的人的戏称。
keywords.example_zh: 作者把前线部署工程师想象成专门协调一群 AI 智能体的人，借这个虚构头衔调侃 2027 年的岗位说明。

keywords.definition_zh: 指深入客户实际业务环境、负责把技术方案落地的工程师。
keywords.example_zh: 作者拿这个真实岗位开玩笑，想象它到 2027 年会变成负责管理智能体群的角色。

keywords.definition_zh: 是对掌控整个智能体群的最高指挥者的戏称。
keywords.example_zh: 在作者虚构的岗位名单里，创始人成了统领一群 AI 智能体的人。

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.headline_zh: 用自己的真实任务给 AI 做评测
builders.headline_en: Make your own work the benchmark for AI

points.zh: 建议建立个人基准测试，用自己经常做的任务衡量 AI 的表现。
points.en: He recommends building a personal benchmark that measures AI performance on tasks you routinely do.

builders.summary_en: Make your own work the benchmark for AI
builders.summary_zh: 用自己的真实任务给 AI 做评测

slang.definition_en: A repeatable AI test based on tasks from your own work.
slang.definition_zh: 用自己工作里的任务组成的可重复 AI 测试。

slang.definition_en: Internet slang for optimizing or leaning hard into something.
slang.definition_zh: 网络用语，指使劲投入、把某件事做到极致。

keywords.definition_zh: 是借用网络后缀「maxxing」来强调把个人化评测做到极致的说法。
keywords.example_zh: 作者用这个玩梗说法鼓励读者把自己的真实工作当成评测材料，再用这些任务判断 AI 是否好用。

keywords.definition_zh: 指根据个人真实任务建立的一套评测基准。
keywords.example_zh: 作者分享了制作这种基准的方法，让读者可以用自己的工作检验 AI 表现。

tweets.text: You need to be personal benchmark maxxing https://t.co/p8owPoAMhP
here's how to make a personal benchmark, courtesy our very own @hammer_mt: https://t.co/aZMpB64xSl

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.headline_zh: 美国的创业环境和资本市场仍让各国创业者向往
builders.headline_en: America's startup ecosystem and capital markets still draw global interest

points.zh: 从海外旅行的见闻出发，认为美国的创业生态和资本市场仍是许多国家与创业者想借鉴的样板。
points.en: Drawing on his travels, he argues that many countries and founders still look to the U.S. startup ecosystem and capital markets as models.

points.zh: 以自己在 Meta 的经历类比 Nvidia，认为有实力的公司挺过生存危机后，往往会采取更强势的竞争策略。
points.en: Drawing on his experience at Meta, he predicts that Nvidia will compete more aggressively after weathering a crisis.

builders.summary_en: America's startup ecosystem and capital markets still draw global interest
builders.summary_zh: 美国的创业环境和资本市场仍让各国创业者向往

slang.definition_en: An AI agent that can initiate work without a fresh user prompt.
slang.definition_zh: 无需用户逐次下达指令，就能主动发起任务的 AI 智能体。

keywords.definition_zh: 指由投资者、资金和融资渠道等构成的资本市场基础。
keywords.example_zh: 作者认为，美国的资本市场基础和创业环境是其他国家及创业者想要效仿的条件。

keywords.definition_zh: 在企业语境中指可能威胁组织存续的危机。
keywords.example_zh: 作者借自己在 Meta 的经历说明，挺过生存危机的公司往往会变得更有进攻性，并用这个判断来谈 Nvidia。

keywords.definition_zh: 是形容一方决心强硬反击或彻底击败对手的口语表达。
keywords.example_zh: 作者用它形容公司挺过生存危机之后的进攻姿态，并推测 Nvidia 接下来会更积极地争夺优势。

tweets.text:
Sometimes you need to travel abroad to deeply appreciate just how inspirational America is to the rest of the world.

Countries and individuals aspire to have an entreprenurial ecosystem like ours. A capital market base like ours.

They don't want to be like China or the UK or Denmark. 

They want to be like America.

And this is particularly true for the most ambitious people in every country. They are students of how America builds.

This doesn't mean we cannot do better ourselves. We must and we will.
tweets.summary_en: America’s startup ecosystem and capital markets remain a model for ambitious entrepreneurs around the world, and the U.S. still has room to improve them.

tweets.text:
This is an agent you don't have to prompt. It's proactive. 

Excited about this launch. https://t.co/KrINO0HQUT

Most good organizations when faced with an existential crisis that doesn’t destroy them will return meaner and out for blood.

They have seen what failure could look like and are ready to go to war to make sure that never happens.

I felt this over and over again at Meta. 

Nvidia isn’t going to hold back now.

builders.name: Claude
builders.headline_zh: Claude 将连接器和技能合为插件，已有逾万个
builders.headline_en: Claude unifies connectors and skills in a catalog of over 10,000 plugins

points.zh: Claude 把连接外部工具的连接器和教 Claude 执行特定任务的技能统一为插件，可浏览逾 1 万个。Free、Pro、Max 和 Ultra 已开放，Team 和 Enterprise 即将跟进。
points.en: Claude has unified connectors for external tools and skills for specific tasks as plugins, with over 10,000 to browse. Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra have access now, with Team and Enterprise coming soon.

points.zh: 支持零数据留存（ZDR）的企业前沿防护（EFS）向符合条件的企业开放公测。该功能与逾 100 家客户共同开发，可在符合零留存要求的同时跨多次请求识别滥用。
points.en: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) with zero data retention (ZDR) is in public beta for eligible businesses. Developed with over 100 customers, it detects misuse across requests while remaining compatible with ZDR.

points.zh: EFS 已支持 Claude Platform、Claude Platform on AWS、Amazon Bedrock 和 Google Cloud 上的 Claude，即将支持 Microsoft Foundry。
points.en: EFS is available on Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Claude on Google Cloud, with Microsoft Foundry support coming soon.

builders.summary_en: Claude unifies connectors and skills in a catalog of over 10,000 plugins
builders.summary_zh: Claude 将连接器和技能合为插件，已有逾万个

slang.definition_en: An integration that lets Claude access an external tool or data source.
slang.definition_zh: 让 Claude 访问外部工具或数据源的集成。

slang.definition_en: Reusable instructions or resources that teach Claude a specific task.
slang.definition_zh: 教 Claude 完成特定任务的可复用指令或资源。

slang.definition_en: An installable extension that can package integrations, skills, or both.
slang.definition_zh: 可安装的扩展，可包含工具连接、技能或两者。

slang.definition_en: Zero data retention, a setting that limits retention of request content.
slang.definition_zh: 零数据留存，按约定不保留请求内容。

slang.definition_en: Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, Claude's enterprise feature for detecting misuse across requests.
slang.definition_zh: 企业前沿防护，用于跨多次请求识别滥用的 Claude 企业功能。

keywords.definition_zh: 指让 AI 接入外部工具或数据源的连接组件。
keywords.example_zh: Claude 把连接器和技能统一放进插件体系，用户可以通过插件接入自己使用的工具。

keywords.definition_zh: 指可以给软件添加功能的扩展组件。
keywords.example_zh: 在这次发布中，Claude 的插件可以接入工具、添加技能，或同时实现这两种功能。

keywords.definition_zh: 指服务处理请求后不保留约定范围内的请求数据。
keywords.example_zh: Claude 宣布，符合条件的企业可以在公开测试中启用零数据留存，同时使用能够跨多次请求识别滥用的防护功能。

tweets.text:
There’s now one way to connect your tools to Claude, teach it a new skill, or do both.

Connectors and skills come together as plugins. Live on Free, Pro, Max, and Ultra plans, with Team and Enterprise coming soon.

Browse 10,000+ plugins: https://t.co/gSwpY9HDPY https://t.co/K78lwls8qh

Zero data retention (ZDR) with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) is now in public beta for eligible businesses. It looks for misuse across many requests while remaining compatible with ZDR.

We developed it with over 100 customers.

Read more: https://t.co/M8riFzHDPY https://t.co/eOonILkHt3
EFS is available on the Claude Platform, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Claude on Google Cloud. Support for EFS in Microsoft Foundry is coming soon.

vocab.definition_en: The point at which a small additional change triggers a much larger shift.
vocab.definition_zh: 临界点，指再增加一点变化就会引发更大转变的时刻或阶段。
vocab.example_en: The third lab’s decision to join was the tipping point for the partnership.
vocab.example_zh: 第三家实验室决定加入，成为促成这项合作的临界点。

vocab.definition_en: To reach the same level or pace as someone or something that has advanced further.
vocab.definition_zh: 赶上，追上已经领先的人或事物。
vocab.example_en: Code review hasn’t caught up with how fast the team can write code.
vocab.example_zh: 代码审查的速度还没跟上团队写代码的速度。

vocab.definition_en: Informally, to keep watching a task or system because it may need frequent attention.
vocab.definition_zh: 口语中指一直盯着某项任务或系统，随时准备处理问题。
vocab.example_en: I used to babysit every pull request until the checks passed.
vocab.example_zh: 以前每个拉取请求我都得一直盯到检查通过。

vocab.definition_en: A person or system entrusted with looking after something over time.
vocab.definition_zh: 管理者或看护者，指受托持续照管某事物的人或系统。
vocab.example_en: The PR steward tracks failed checks and follows up on fixes.
vocab.example_zh: 拉取请求管理工具会追踪未通过的检查，并跟进修复。

vocab.definition_en: To make a new product, feature, or change available, often in stages.
vocab.definition_zh: 推出、上线，常指分阶段向用户开放产品、功能或更新。
vocab.example_en: We’ll roll out the feature to a small group of users first.
vocab.example_zh: 我们会先向一小批用户开放这项功能。

vocab.definition_en: To apply a targeted update that fixes a software defect or vulnerability.
vocab.definition_zh: 给软件打补丁，通过局部更新修复缺陷或安全漏洞。
vocab.example_en: The maintainers patched the flaw before the next release.
vocab.example_zh: 维护人员在下一个版本发布前修复了这个缺陷。

vocab.definition_en: A weakness or defect in how something is designed, built, or reasoned.
vocab.definition_zh: 缺陷、瑕疵或漏洞，可指设计、实现或推理中的薄弱之处。
vocab.example_en: The team found a flaw in the approval process during testing.
vocab.example_zh: 团队在测试中发现了审批流程中的一个缺陷。

vocab.definition_en: Prone to software errors or unexpected behavior.
vocab.definition_zh: 软件错误较多的，运行时容易出现异常的。
vocab.example_en: The beta feels buggy when several tasks run at once.
vocab.example_zh: 同时运行多个任务时，这个测试版容易出问题。

quote.text_en: Trust grows one verified improvement at a time.
quote.text_zh: 每一次经得起验证的改进，都让信任多一点。
quote.author: Original

slang_glossary.definition_en: Respond to a request, challenge, or need by taking action.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 响应号召，或在有需求时采取行动。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An intensely devoted fan. As a verb, it means to enthusiastically support someone.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 铁粉。作动词时指热烈追捧或支持某人。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The threshold after which a larger change takes hold.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 触发更大变化的临界点。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for laboratory, used here for an AI research or model development organization.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: laboratory 的简称，此处指从事 AI 研究或模型开发的机构。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The name of a cryptocurrency exchange referenced in the post.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 帖子提及的一家加密货币交易所的名称。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The initials of Sam Bankman-Fried.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 萨姆·班克曼-弗里德姓名的首字母缩写。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A trained AI system that can perform tasks such as generating text or code.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 经过训练、能够执行生成文本或代码等任务的 AI 模型。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Release software or get a change through to delivery.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 发布软件，或推动一项变更走完交付流程。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Pull request, a proposal to review and merge code changes in a repository.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: pull request 的缩写，即拉取请求，用于提议审查并合并代码变更。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A prerelease stage in which users can try a product or feature while it is still being tested.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 测试阶段，产品或功能在继续测试期间已向部分或全部用户开放试用。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In this context, the pace at which a developer or team delivers work.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 此处指开发人员或团队交付工作的速度。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Examining proposed code changes to find problems and assess whether they are ready to merge.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 代码审查，检查拟议的代码变更，发现问题并判断是否可以合并。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Keep monitoring pull requests, checking their status and stepping in when something stalls or fails.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 一直盯着拉取请求的进展，在卡住或检查失败时介入处理。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A person or tool that keeps pull requests moving by following up on fixes and failed checks.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 负责跟进修复和失败检查、推动拉取请求继续处理的人或工具。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Automated checks that have reported a failure, such as tests or lint checks.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 未通过的自动检查，例如自动化测试或代码规范检查。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Authorizations that allow a proposed change or action to proceed under applicable rules.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 审批，即按适用规则授权某项拟议变更或操作继续进行。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A slash command mentioned in the post for invoking a software delivery workflow.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 帖子中提到的斜杠命令，用于调用软件交付流程。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for administrator, someone with permission to manage settings or access.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: administrator 的简称，指有权管理设置或访问权限的管理员。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Short for repository, a project’s files and version history.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: repository 的简称，即存放项目文件和版本历史的代码仓库。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A mode that shows or records what an automation would do without carrying out those actions.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 观察模式，展示或记录自动化系统原本会采取的操作，但不实际执行。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The process of making a feature or update available, often gradually.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 功能或更新的上线过程，通常分阶段开放。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The name used in the posts for an OpenAI agent system and for individual agents within it.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 帖子中对 OpenAI 一套智能体系统及其中单个智能体的称呼。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A targeted software fix, or the act of applying one.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 软件补丁，也可指给软件打补丁的操作。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Open-source software, whose source code is available under a license that permits use, modification, and distribution.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: open-source software 的缩写，即开源软件。其许可证允许使用、修改和分发源代码。

slang_glossary.definition_en: The underlying systems, services, and tools that applications depend on.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 基础设施，指应用所依赖的底层系统、服务和工具。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An informal spelling of kind of, meaning somewhat or to some degree.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: kind of 的口语写法，表示「有点」或「多少有些」。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A mildly vulgar abbreviation for bullshit, used to call something absurd, unfair, or untrue.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: bullshit 的缩写，略带粗口色彩，可用来吐槽某事离谱、不公平或不可信。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A period before a social-media handle, traditionally used on Twitter to make a post that begins with a mention read as a public post.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在社交媒体账号名前加一个句点。Twitter 上传统用法是让以提及他人开头的帖子作为公开发帖来阅读。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Having frequent or noticeable software errors.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 软件运行不稳定，容易出现错误或异常。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Giving an AI model instructions, questions, examples, or context to guide its output.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 向 AI 模型提供指令、问题、示例或背景，以引导输出。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A small central group responsible for the project’s essential work.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 精简的核心团队，人数少，负责项目的关键工作。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A group of AI agents that work together, often handling different tasks in parallel.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 智能体集群，由多个 AI 智能体协作，常并行处理不同任务。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Empirical relationships between model performance and factors such as model size, training data, and compute.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 规模定律，描述模型表现与模型规模、训练数据量和算力等因素之间的经验关系。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Using more computation when generating an answer to try to improve its quality.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 推理时扩展，即在生成答案时投入更多算力，以尝试提升答案质量。

slang_glossary.definition_en: AI capabilities developed or operated under a country’s own control, often with domestic infrastructure or data governance.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 主权 AI，指由一国自主掌控的 AI 能力，通常涉及本国基础设施或数据治理。

slang_glossary.definition_en: AI whose trained model weights are available for download and use under the applicable license terms.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 开放权重 AI，指可按适用许可条款下载并使用其训练后模型权重的 AI。

slang_glossary.definition_en: AI systems at the leading edge of current capabilities.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 前沿 AI，指能力处于当前领先水平的 AI 系统。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An evaluation of an AI system using tasks and criteria tailored to an individual’s needs.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 个人评测，即用符合自身需求的任务和标准来评价 AI 系统。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An AI system that works toward a goal by choosing actions, often using tools over several steps.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: AI 智能体，能够围绕目标选择行动，常通过多步操作和工具调用完成工作。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Keep generating follow-up instructions for itself to continue or refine work.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在循环中不断为自己生成后续指令，以继续或改进工作。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A dismissive term for low-quality or careless AI-generated content, especially when produced in bulk.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 带贬义的说法，指粗制滥造的 AI 生成内容，尤其是批量产出的低质量内容。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In agent discussions, shorthand for a coordinated group of agents working together.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在智能体语境中，指协同工作的智能体集群。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An engineer who works directly with customers to adapt, integrate, and deploy a product in their environment.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 前线部署工程师，直接与客户合作，在客户环境中适配、集成和部署产品。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A repeatable test based on someone’s own tasks, used to compare tools or track changes in performance.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 个人基准测试，用自己的任务设计可重复的测试，以比较工具或追踪表现变化。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Internet slang for trying to optimize or maximize a particular trait, activity, or outcome.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 网络俚语，指努力把某种特质、活动或结果优化到极致，常作为后缀使用。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An agent designed to identify and initiate useful actions without waiting for a new prompt each time.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 主动式智能体，能够自行识别并发起有用的行动，无须每次等待新的指令。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An integration that lets an app or agent access another service, its data, or its functions.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 连接器，用于让应用或智能体接入外部服务及其数据或功能。

slang_glossary.definition_en: A reusable set of instructions or capabilities that helps an agent perform a specific kind of task.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 技能，为智能体提供执行某类任务所需的可复用指令或能力。

slang_glossary.definition_en: An add-on that extends a host application with features, integrations, or tools.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 插件，为宿主应用增加功能、集成或工具的扩展组件。

slang_glossary.definition_en: Zero Data Retention, a policy or configuration under which specified data is not retained after processing.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: Zero Data Retention 的缩写，即零数据保留，指指定范围内的数据在处理后不被留存。

slang_glossary.definition_en: In AWS contexts, Elastic File System, a managed shared file storage service. The supplied sample does not establish which expansion is intended.
slang_glossary.definition_zh: 在 AWS 语境下通常指 Elastic File System，即托管式共享文件存储服务。所给样本未交代这里的具体含义。
